Common Cold.summary: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat. Most people recover on their own within about a week to ten days.
seek_care: Difficulty breathing or wheezing
A high fever that does not settle
Symptoms lasting longer than about 10 days or getting worse
Symptoms in a young infant, an older adult or someone with a long-term condition
general_notes: Rest and fluids are generally encouraged.
Washing hands often reduces the spread of colds.

Influenza.summary: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. It tends to start suddenly with fever and body aches, and can lead to serious complications in some people.
seek_care: Trouble breathing or chest pain
Confusion or severe drowsiness
Vomiting that will not stop
Getting better and then suddenly worse
general_notes: Yearly influenza vaccination is the main preventive measure.
Staying home while unwell helps protect others.

Allergic Rhinitis.summary: Inflammation of the lining of the nose triggered by allergens such as pollen, dust mites or pet dander.
seek_care: Wheezing or shortness of breath
Symptoms that disturb sleep or daily life
Uncertainty about what is triggering the symptoms
general_notes: Identifying and reducing contact with triggers is a key step.
A clinician can help confirm the cause.

Migraine.summary: A neurological condition causing recurring headaches, often on one side of the head, frequently with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound.
seek_care: A sudden, extremely severe headache unlike any before
Headache with weakness, numbness, vision loss or difficulty speaking
Headache with fever and a stiff neck
Headache after a head injury
general_notes: Keeping a headache diary can help identify patterns and triggers.
Regular sleep, meals and hydration are commonly discussed with clinicians.

Gastroenteritis.summary: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by a viral or bacterial infection or by contaminated food or water.
seek_care: Signs of dehydration: very dry mouth, little urine, dizziness
Blood in stool or vomit
High fever or symptoms lasting more than a few days
Illness in infants, older adults or pregnant women
general_notes: Keeping up fluid intake is important.
Hand washing and safe food handling reduce the risk of infection.

Urinary Tract Infection.summary: An infection of part of the urinary system, most often the bladder.
typical_features: Burning or pain when passing urine
seek_care: Fever, chills or pain in the back or side
Blood in the urine
Symptoms during pregnancy or in children and men
Symptoms that return often
general_notes: A clinician can confirm the cause, usually with a simple urine test.
Staying hydrated is generally encouraged.

Pneumonia.summary: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs. It can range from mild to life-threatening.
typical_features: Chest pain when breathing or coughing
seek_care: Any difficulty breathing
Chest pain
Confusion or bluish lips
Symptoms in infants, older adults or people with chronic illness
general_notes: Pneumonia needs medical assessment; it should not be self-managed.
Vaccination, not smoking and good hand hygiene lower the risk.

Dengue.summary: A mosquito-borne viral infection found in tropical and subtropical regions.
typical_features: Severe headache and pain behind the eyes
seek_care: Severe stomach pain or persistent vomiting
Bleeding from the nose or gums, or blood in vomit or stool
Extreme tiredness or restlessness
Worsening symptoms around the time the fever falls
general_notes: Ask a clinician before taking any medicine for suspected dengue.
Avoiding mosquito bites and removing standing water helps prevent spread.

Typhoid.summary: A bacterial infection (Salmonella Typhi) spread through contaminated food or water.
seek_care: Any suspected case should be assessed by a clinician and tested
Severe abdominal pain, confusion or bleeding needs urgent care
general_notes: Safe drinking water, careful food hygiene and hand washing reduce risk.
Vaccines exist and are recommended in some regions.

Asthma.summary: A long-term condition in which the airways become inflamed and narrow, making breathing difficult at times.
typical_features: Cough, often worse at night or with exercise
seek_care: Severe breathlessness or difficulty speaking in full sentences
Blue lips or fingertips
Symptoms that do not improve with the plan agreed with your clinician
general_notes: People with asthma usually work with a clinician on a written action plan.
Identifying personal triggers can help.
